summary: The audit checks the 60 units of the major: CSRE 100, two of the three Comparative Core courses, one Methodology course of 3 or more units, the Community-Engaged Learning course (which can be a course that also counts elsewhere), CSRE 200X or 201X for the WIM and capstone, 15 units in your subplan and electives from the CCSRE family of programs. At most 15 of your elective and subplan units can come from AFRICAAM, ASNAMST, CHILATST, JEWISHST and NATIVEAM courses (a CSRE course cross-listed there counts too). The core, Methodology, WIM and capstone courses need a letter grade and a C- or better; electives and subplan courses need a letter grade (D- or better) unless the course is only offered S/NC. You check by hand that no more than two elective or subplan classes are S/NC, that subplan courses fit the subplan's focus, petitioned courses from outside CCSRE (at most 15 units), a CEL fellowship or Alternative Spring Break, and for honors the proposal, the 3.7 major and 3.5 overall GPA and the B+ thesis grade.

totals.label: At most 15 units of AFRICAAM, ASNAMST, CHILATST, JEWISHST and NATIVEAM courses
totals.why: "CSRE majors may count up to 15 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Asian American Studies (ASNAMST), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Jewish Studies (JEWISHST), or Native American Studies (NATIVEAM) courses toward their elective coursework in the CSRE major (including subplan units)." The elective rule caps its own share; this cap covers the electives and subplan together. A CSRE course cross-listed in one of these subjects also counts against it.

program.why: Grading: "All courses must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC." "Student may count 2 classes with Satisfactory/No Credit (SNC) grading basis toward Additional Units" names courses offered only S/NC (their grading basis), which the audit accepts under the letter-grade rule; the two-class limit is checked by hand.

bTVtrrs4.why: "The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by courses that also fulfill other CSRE degree requirements (e.g., a Methodology course may also count toward the CEL requirement)." A Cardinal Course, CCSRE fellowship or Alternative Spring Break not on the list ("may be fulfilled by academic experiences ... that do not carry academic units") is marked done by hand. Grading: "All courses must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC." The two S/NC classes the text allows count toward Additional Units, not toward CEL.

SP4Qc5jl.why: "CSRE majors must complete the remaining units of their 60-unit minimum with elective coursework in the CCSRE family of programs, with the exception below. CSRE majors may count up to 15 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Asian American Studies (ASNAMST), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Jewish Studies (JEWISHST), or Native American Studies (NATIVEAM) courses toward their elective coursework in the CSRE major (including subplan units)." The Bulletin's 60-unit program minimum covers the rest; this rule asks for the least that can remain: 60 minus CSRE 100 (5), the Comparative Core (15), Methodology (at most 5), the WIM/capstone course (5) and the subplan (15) is 15. The 15-unit cap is shared with the subplan in the Bulletin but applies to this rule alone here, and it also counts a CSRE course cross-listed in those subjects (CSRE 4 is also AFRICAAM 4); the text does not say whether a cross-listed course counts against the cap.

4JtRcCwB.why: "Honors students must apply with a complete proposal approved by a CCSRE faculty advisor in the spring preceding their final year of study. Honors students must continuously enroll at Stanford in autumn, winter, and spring." "Honors applications are open to students with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall. Students must receive a B+ or above on their thesis and maintain the GPA minimum until graduation in order to receive Honors."

add.why: "Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major.
